subject.title: cli-backend: stale systemSent on session entries survives gateway restart — fresh spawns (esp. after /new) run WITHOUT the agent system prompt (identity loss)

question: Does a managed current-main Claude CLI run prove that gateway restart plus `/new`, and restart without `/new`, both preserve the agent system prompt before this issue is closed as implemented?
rationale: Source inspection indicates the stale `systemSent` gate is no longer authoritative, but the reported shipped failure crosses persisted state, live stdio process ownership, and Claude resume behavior; source-only inference cannot safely substitute for the requested live proof and fix provenance.

options.title: Run both restart scenarios
options.body: Validate current main with a real Claude CLI session, covering restart plus `/new` and restart with native resume or fresh fallback, then identify the responsible commit and release status.

options.title: Keep for a narrow repair
options.body: If either scenario still loses identity, patch the CLI-session ownership boundary and add focused restart/reset regression tests without adding configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Run both restart scenarios
recommendation.body: Validate current main with a real Claude CLI session, covering restart plus `/new` and restart with native resume or fresh fallback, then identify the responsible commit and release status.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior reset-time CLI-binding work and tests are the closest established ownership signal for this lifecycle invariant.
